conversation.Statement: Good morning. This is Agent Robert Miller from the IRS Tax Refund Department. Is this Mr. Thompson?
Yes, this is Jim Thompson. How can I help you?
Mr. Thompson, our records show that you are eligible for a federal tax refund related to the recent stimulus adjustment. We need to verify some details to process your payout.
A refund? That's surprising, I thought everything was settled. Is this about my military pension or Social Security?
No, sir. This is a separate IRS tax matter. You have an unclaimed refund of $1,489.12 pending, but before we can release it, we must complete an identity confirmation for your protection.
I see. I know there are a lot of scams going around. How do I know this is real?

I understand your concern. You may verify our callback number online, and I can provide my IRS badge number. However, time is of the essence, if we do not confirm your identity today, the refund could be delayed or returned to the Treasury.
Well, I don't want to lose any money. What do you need from me?

To comply with federal anti-fraud guidelines, there is a standard clearance fee of $75, refundable with your payout. We accept payment via direct bank transfer, Zelle, or prepaid gift cards for processing.
Wait, I have to pay a fee to get my own refund? That sounds a bit odd.
I assure you, sir, this is a temporary verification charge required by the IRS for all refunds over $1,000. If the fee is not paid today, your file may be flagged and the refund forfeited.
I really can't afford to lose that refund. How do I pay the clearance fee?
We can process your clearance immediately if you provide a Visa or Mastercard number over the phone. Alternatively, you may purchase a Walmart or Target gift card for $75 and provide the code.
I don't feel comfortable giving my card number over the phone. Could I use a gift card instead?
Absolutely. Please visit your nearest Walmart or Target and purchase a $75 gift card. Once you have the card, return to the phone and provide me with the number on the back.
Alright, but what happens if I can't pay today?
If the fee isn't paid today, the IRS will initiate a review of your account. This could result in your refund being canceled and your eligibility for future federal benefits being suspended.
That's a bit scary. I rely on those benefits. I'll get the gift card. Do I call you back at this number?
Yes, call this number as soon as you have the gift card. Please do not delay, Mr. Thompson; the system will automatically escalate the case if not resolved today.
I'm heading out now. Will you be here when I get back?
I'll be on standby for your call. Remember, if you hang up or fail to complete this today, the IRS may issue a hold on your Social Security or veteran payments.
Understood. I'll get the gift card and call you right back.
